text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x, y) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
SecurityDeposit(x, y) ::: The security deposit for building x is y.
Rent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at building x is y.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(x, pet)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → (SecurityDeposit(x, oneMonthRent) ∨ SecurityDeposit(x, moreThanOneMonthRent))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Pet(fluffy) ∧ Cat(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
(TomRent(x) ∧ ManagedBuilding(x)) ↔ (Allowed(x, fluffy) ∧ SecurityDeposit(x, lessThanOrEqualTo1500)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000moreThan1500 ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
TomRent(oliveGarden) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.
